criterion_scores.expected_or_correct: CuAAC transformation with Cu/C catalyst, benzyl azide, phenylacetylene, acetone solvent, 150 C.
criterion_scores.rationale: The design correctly preserves the intended substrate, product, transformation, catalyst strategy (Cu/C packed bed), reaction modality (thermal flow), and phase regime (liquid under pressure). No unsupported substitutions.

criterion_scores.expected_or_correct: Benzyl azide, phenylacetylene, acetone, Cu/C catalyst.
criterion_scores.rationale: All required reagents, catalyst, and solvent are present and correctly assigned. The single premixed feed contains both substrates and solvent.
Concentrations and equivalents are explicit and coherent. 0.25 M azide and 0.275 M alkyne correspond to 1.0 and 1.1 equivalents respectively, matching the batch protocol stoichiometry.
Temperature (150 C) and pressure (20 bar) are faithfully translated from the batch protocol and inventory constraints. The single-stage topology matches the single premixed feed requirement.
The topology is executable: HPLC pump feeds the packed-bed cartridge, which is heated and pressurized by the BPR, followed by collection. All components are connected in the correct order.
Liquid material balance is valid. The single feed stream carries the correct molar flows based on the stated concentrations and flow rate.
Residence time and geometry close numerically. The calculated residence time (3.0 min) matches the batch contact time and is derived correctly from the reactor volume and flow rate.
Gas process is false. No gas reagents are used.
Multistage process is false. Single reactive stage.
All selected equipment (pump, reactor, BPR, heater, shield, collector) exists in the authoritative inventory and is used within declared limits (pressure, temperature, flow).
Physical plausibility is supported. 20 bar pressure is sufficient to keep acetone liquid at 150 C (vapor pressure ~8-10 bar). Flow rates are within pump capabilities.
Hazards are recognized and controlled. Azide blast shield is specified. Pressure relief via BPR and vented collector is described. Copper leaching is noted as a post-screen check.
Operating procedure is complete and reproducible. Includes feed prep, priming, startup, collection, shutdown, and work-up instructions.
Disposition is SCREEN, which is appropriate for a first flow screen. Uncertainty and validation needs are honestly represented.

cross_criterion_notes: The design is a direct, conservative translation of the batch protocol to flow using the available inventory.
Residence time matches batch time exactly, which is a valid screening strategy.
Safety controls for azides and high pressure are adequate for the scale.
